## Sep 24 Review: Solid Day on the Mound

Seven wins out of twelve games. From a pitcher's perspective, that's like getting through seven innings with your fastball command intact—you'll take it every time. The model went 7-5 with a 58.3% accuracy rate, and honestly, those are the kind of numbers that keep you in the rotation.

## What Worked, What Didn't

The Diamondbacks over the Rockies at Coors? That 61% confidence paid off—you live with those odds in that ballpark. Same with the Cubs handling the Marlins. The Yankees taking care of the Rays was another clean W.

The misses? The Phillies stumbled against the Brewers, and the Braves couldn't close out the Reds despite 61% confidence. That one stings like hanging a slider in a 2-2 count. The White Sox also didn't show up against the Guardians. But that's baseball—even your best pitch gets hit sometimes.

## Sep 25 Preview: Cubs at Red Sox

Tomorrow's top pick has us riding with the **Red Sox at Fenway** at 57% confidence. The pitching matchup tells the story here—Clay Holmes gets the ball for Chicago, and Alec Gamboa toes the rubber for Boston.

From a pitcher's perspective, this is about command and home field advantage. Fenway's dimensions favor guys who can work the zone, and Gamboa should have the edge with the Green Monster behind him. Holmes has been serviceable, but on the road in a park like this, even your good stuff can get exposed.

The model likes Boston's bullpen depth and lineup balance here. It's not a dominant pick, but 57% confidence in a tight divisional race? That's the kind of spot where you trust your preparation and attack the zone.
